summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).
authority_html:
- **VICAA (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — federal-facility reporting mandates  
- **ICWA (25 U.S.C. §§ 1901–1963)** — tribal jurisdiction, placement preferences, notice to tribes

primary_citations.citation_text: Vermont - 33 V.S.A. Chapter 49 (Child Welfare Services – § 4913 mandatory reporting)
Vermont - 33 V.S.A. Chapter 53 (Children in Need of Care or Supervision — CHINS proceedings in the Family Division of the Superior Court)
Title 33: Human Services - DCF - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

regulations_applicable.title: Vermont DCF Family Services Division rules and policy manual (Rule 2000 Response to Child Abuse and Neglect; Rule 3000 Administrative Review Process; Rule 7000 Transition Age Youth)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court remanded for ICWA notice to the Mohawk Tribe because the trial court had reason to believe an Indian child was involved, and otherwise affirmed the CHINS merits and disposition orders, holding the preponderance standard governs a CHINS adjudication and that merits and disposition orders must rest on findings of fact.
key_cases.relevance: This is Vermont's first ICWA decision; it requires the court itself to notify a tribe once it has reason to believe an Indian child is involved, and it construes the 'Indian child' and 'Indian tribe' definitions.
key_cases.quote: the standard of proof for a CHINS adjudication is that the findings be supported by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.holding: The termination case was remanded for notice to the Bureau of Indian Affairs because the court itself had a duty to give ICWA notice once information in a court-ordered evaluation gave it reason to believe the children were of Indian ancestry.
key_cases.relevance: J.T. places the ICWA notice duty on the Vermont family court, not only on the petitioning party, and triggers it on information already in the court's own record.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the trial court had a duty to provide notice once it had reason to believe the children were of Indian ancestry.

key_cases.holding: No ICWA notice was required where the asserted tribes, the Abenaki and Micmac, are not federally recognized, and excluding non-recognized tribes from ICWA does not violate equal protection.
key_cases.relevance: This is the decisive Vermont case for practitioners, because the tribes most often asserted in Vermont, the Abenaki and Micmac, lack federal recognition and therefore do not trigger ICWA.
key_cases.quote: we agree with the court's conclusion in T.I.S. that the ICWA exclusion of non-recognized tribes does not violate the Equal Protection Clause

key_cases.holding: The family division had reason to know K.S. might be an Indian child once a parent reported Cherokee heritage on the record, but after notice was given and the tribes responded, the determination that K.S. was not an Indian child was affirmed along with the termination order.
key_cases.relevance: K.S. applies the 2016 federal ICWA regulations in Vermont, holding that a participant's statement of tribal heritage anywhere in the record, including a permanency case plan, triggers the inquiry and notice duty.
key_cases.quote: father's statement was sufficient to give the court reason to know that K.S. was an Indian child for purposes of the ICWA

search_keywords: Vermont Department for Children and Families

state_agency.name: Vermont Department for Children and Families, Family Services Division

mandatory_reporters: Health care providers, including physicians, surgeons, osteopaths, chiropractors, physician assistants, resident physicians, interns, hospital administrators, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, medical examiners, emergency medical personnel, dentists, psychologists, and pharmacists — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(1)

School district and approved or recognized independent school employees, and contracted student-services providers, including superintendents, headmasters, teachers, student teachers, school librarians, principals, and guidance counselors — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(2)
Agency of Human Services employees, contractors, and grantees who have contact with clients — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(7)
Camp owners (“camp” includes any residential or nonresidential recreational program, 33 V.S.A. § 4913(b)) — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(9)
Members of the clergy, except information received while acting as a spiritual advisor in a confidential communication (33 V.S.A. § 4913(j)) — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(12)
Employees of the Office of the Child, Youth, and Family Advocate — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(13)
reporting_details: Vermont is not a universal-reporting state: the 13 categories of mandated reporters listed in 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a) must report to DCF within 24 hours of the time the information was first received or observed, and any other concerned person may report voluntarily (33 V.S.A. § 4913(c), (e)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 72 hours to begin an assessment or investigation
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the report, once accepted as a valid allegation and there is sufficient information to proceed
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The Commissioner may waive the 72-hour requirement only when necessary to locate the child or to ensure the safety of the child or social worker (33 V.S.A. § 4915(b)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 45 days (assessment track); no statutory deadline (investigation track)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An assessment may be extended only upon written justification by the Department and not beyond 60 days total (33 V.S.A. § 4915a(b)); Vermont sets no completion deadline for the investigation track (33 V.S.A. § 4915b).
